parts.latex: Find the minimum time needed to complete the project.

solutions.latex:
The float time of $I$ is the latest start time minus the earliest start time minus the duration.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Float time of } I &= 17-7-5 \\ &= 5 \text{ minutes} \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
A project requires activities A to F to be completed. The activity chart shows the immediate prerequisites and duration for each activity.

\exfigure{1266_q39_1}

A new activity, $X$, is added to the project, and has $A$ as an immediate prerequisite. No other activity has $X$ as an immediate prerequisite.

By first drawing a network diagram showing all seven activities, find the maximum duration of $X$ if it does not increase the minimum time to complete the project.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{1266_q39_s1}

From the network diagram, the critical path of the original activities is $A, C, D, E$, with a minimum project time of 15 minutes.

$X$ has $A$ as its immediate prerequisite, so it cannot start until $A$ finishes, at 6 minutes. No activity depends on $X$, so draw an edge from $X$ to the End.

For the project time to stay at 15 minutes, $X$ must finish by 15 minutes, starting at 6 minutes.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Maximum duration} &= 15 - 6 \\ &= 9 \text{ minutes} \end{aligned}$$

solutions.latex:
Delaying activity $I$ by $10$ hours makes it start at $16+10=26$.

It takes $7$ hours, so it finishes at $26+7=33$.

This is within the latest allowed time, so the project finish is not delayed: $0$ hours.

Hence the correct option is the one equal to $0$.

parts.latex:
Ryan is building a new shed. The project involves activities A to E.

The network diagram shows these activities and their completion times in days.

\exfigure{3300_qD13_1}

Which activities have a float time greater than zero?

solutions.latex:
B, the dummy activity, C and E form the critical path, so their float is zero.

A and D are not on the critical path, so they have float greater than zero.

\exfigure{3300_qD13_s1}

Hence the answer is A.

7359.stem:
Details relating to the last activity ($A_9$) of a building project involving 9 activities, is shown below.

\exfigure{235_q23_1}

figures.cap: activity box legend with A9: duration 8, EST 12, LST 12
activities A7, A8 leading to A9, late start times blank

parts.latex: Explain why this activity is on the critical path of the project.
What is the expected duration of the project?
Explain why activity $A_8$ has a float time.

solutions.latex:
For $A_9$ the early start time and late start time are equal ($12 = 12$).

So its float time is $12 - 12 = 0$, meaning any delay to $A_9$ delays the whole project. Hence it is on the critical path.

The project finishes when the last activity $A_9$ finishes.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Duration} &= \text{EST} + \text{duration of } A_9 \\ &= 12 + 8 \\ &= 20 \text{ days} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the expected duration is } 20 \text{ days}$$

In backward scanning, an activity's late start time is the late start time of the activity that follows it, minus its own duration.

Both $A_7$ and $A_8$ lead into $A_9$, whose LST is $12$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{LST}(A_7) &= 12 - 4 = 8 \\ \text{LST}(A_8) &= 12 - 3 = 9 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{late start of } A_7 = 8 \text{ days, late start of } A_8 = 9 \text{ days}$$

meta.generated_note: Generated solution; values to be written in the lower boxes of A7 and A8.

solutions.latex:
Float time is $\text{LST} - \text{EST}$.

For $A_8$:
$$\text{float} = 9 - 4 = 5 \text{ days}$$
The float is not zero, so $A_8$ can start up to 5 days later than its earliest time without delaying the project.

meta.self_check: LST 9 from part (c), EST 4 from the diagram.
